A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concepts of confounding and collapsibility can only be defined in the context of a model for causal effects.

, in the context of a counterfactual causal model, a confounding variable is a variable that is associated with both treatment and outcome, is a variable that affects the treatment assignment mechanism, and is a variable that, when conditioned on, can affect the association between treatment and outcome.
, in observational studies, confound ing is a property of the data-generating process, collapsibility is a property of a statistical model, and exchangeability is a property of an analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
confounding is not collapsibility and that collapsibility is not a property of confounding, but a property of the model.
confounding is not a binary phenomenon, but rather a matter of degree.
